root_cause.text: The `ivpu_ipc_receive` function in the Intel VPU driver incorrectly casts the firmware-supplied unsigned 32-bit `data_size` to a signed integer using `min_t(int, ...)`, causing large values to be treated as negative and resulting in an unsigned wraparound when assigned to a `u32` variable.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff replaces `u32 size = min_t(int, rx_msg->ipc_hdr->data_size, sizeof(*jsm_msg));` with `u32 size = min(rx_msg->ipc_hdr->data_size, sizeof(*jsm_msg));` in `drivers/accel/ivpu/ivpu_ipc.c` to prevent the signed cast of the unsigned `data_size` parameter.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `ivpu_ipc_receive` contains the vulnerable statement on line 281: `u32 size = min_t(int, rx_msg->ipc_hdr->data_size, sizeof(*jsm_msg));`. This uses `min_t(int, ...)` which casts the firmware-controlled `data_size` (a `u32`) to a signed `int`. If `data_size` is large enough to be negative when cast to `int`, `min_t` will select it as the minimum, and assigning it back to `u32 size` will cause an unsigned wraparound, leading to an out-of-bounds `memcpy` on line 290.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `ivpu_ipc_receive` contains the vulnerable construct on line 247: `u32 size = min_t(int, rx_msg->ipc_hdr->data_size, sizeof(*ipc_payload));`. This incorrectly casts the unsigned `data_size` to a signed `int`, which can result in a negative value being returned by `min_t` if `data_size` is large. This negative value is then assigned to the unsigned `u32 size` variable, causing a wraparound to a large positive integer, which leads to a buffer overflow in the subsequent `memcpy` on line 255.
